content_metadata.description: A detailed analysis of excretion in different animal groups, presented by a lecturer.

qAndA.question: What are the tiny air sacs found in the lungs called?
What is the name of the excretory organ in annelids?

qAndA.answer: Through a process called counter-current flow of water.
qAndA.question: How are waste products removed from the gills of fish?

qAndA.answer: They give birth to live young and they have mammary glands.
qAndA.question: What are two reasons why an animal is considered a mammal?

qAndA.answer: This is because higher organisms have many cells and tissues that produce a lot of waste. Diffusion alone cannot effectively remove this large amount of waste.
qAndA.question: The lecturer mentions that higher organisms require more complex excretory systems. Why is this the case?
